title: Ethiopian Stuffed Eggs
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Stuffed Eggs — hard-boiled eggs halved with yolks mixed with berbere, mitmita, silsi, and coriander. The Ethiopian devilled egg — where Western versions are mild and creamy, the Ethiopian version is fierce and fragrant.
longDesc: Ethiopian stuffed eggs take the universal party food and make it completely Ethiopian — the yolk filling is mixed with berbere, mitmita, and silsi instead of mayonnaise and mustard, producing a devilled egg of heat and complexity.
steps: Mash yolks with berbere, mitmita, silsi, lemon, and oil until smooth.
Garnish with a pinch of mitmita and coriander.
chefTips: The filling should be much drier than standard devilled egg — no mayonnaise.
The mitmita garnish is the visual signature.
commonMistakes: Adding mayo — loses the Ethiopian character.
cookingScience: The egg yolk's emulsifying properties (lecithin) still work without mayonnaise — the small amount of oil and lemon juice create a stable mixture with the yolk proteins. The berbere's fat-soluble compounds dissolve into the yolk fat for uniform distribution.
culturalNote: Ethiopian stuffed eggs demonstrate the Ethiopian cook's instinct — to take any format and apply the berbere tradition to it. The result is always more interesting and more satisfying than the original.
